extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies (lead and cooperating agencies), agency counsel, CEQ staff, and practitioners implementing NEPA reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and best-practice guidance for identifying lead and cooperating agencies, preparing environmental documents, and conducting public and governmental engagement under NEPA. Covers roles/responsibilities, timelines, joint documents, use of cooperating-agency analyses, outreach/notification, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation and compliance plan when EA relies on mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Require agencies to prepare a monitoring and compliance plan when an EA relies on mitigation as a component of the proposed action (consistent with §1505.3(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency assumes as part of its analysis that mitigation will occur and will be effective, the agency must prepare a mitigation and compliance plan for enforceable mitigation and any other mitigation required by §1505.3(c) to ensure the assumption is correct. This is intended to effectuate NEPA's purpose (section 101) and ensure mitigation commitments are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency supervisory responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A lead agency must supervise the preparation of any EIS or EA for an action or group of actions involving more than one Federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §1501.7(a) revised to eliminate reference to 'complex' EAs (term undefined); longstanding paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) retained to describe situations with more than one Federal agency. Lead agency supervision applies generally when more than one Federal agency is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of undefined 'complex EA' concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not retain 'complex EA' in regulations because it was undefined and unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ removed the reference after comment that it was confusing; if retained it would need a clear definition, but the existing lead-agency supervision language already covers multi-agency situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint lead agency invitation/acceptance and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal, State, Tribal, or local agencies may serve as a joint lead agency upon invitation from the Federal lead agency and acceptance by the invited agency; joint lead agencies must fulfill the role of a lead agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retains Federal agencies in the list of potential joint lead agencies because another Federal agency serving as joint lead can enhance efficiency. While generally there will be only one joint lead agency, the regulations are not intended to be restrictive. Agencies often use MOUs or letters/memoranda to outline roles and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining lead and cooperating agencies; factors consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Federal agencies must determine which agency will be the lead agency (considering the factors in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(5)), and the lead agency determines any cooperating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added an explicit clause to clarify that agencies should consider the enumerated factors in making the lead agency determination (the factors appear in (c)(1)-(c)(5)). This is consistent with section 107(a)(1) of NEPA and §1506.2(c) on joint EISs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency ultimate responsibility (but may share)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead agency is ultimately responsible for the NEPA review, though it may share responsibilities with a joint lead agency if designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text clarifies lead agency is ultimately responsible; agencies should communicate roles and points of contact with project proponents. See §1501.10(a) for setting deadlines and schedules and §1500.5(g) indicating all agencies are responsible for meeting deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for lead agency designation and CEQ notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Federal, State, Tribal, or local agency or a person substantially affected by a lack of lead agency designation may submit a request for designation to a participating Federal agency; the receiving agency must provide a copy of such a request to CEQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aligns with section 107(a)(4) of NEPA. CEQ also standardized terminology (replaced 'private person' with 'person').

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and calculation rules for disagreements/designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify timing calculations and deadlines when Federal agencies cannot agree on lead agency designation: 45 days calculated from the date of the written request to senior agency officials; change 'within 20 days' to 'no later than 20 days' in first sentence of paragraph (f); change second-sentence timing to 40 days for CEQ designation (with ‘designate’ language); CEQ's 40-day deadline runs from the date of request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule strikes 'and all responses to it' to clarify the 40-day deadline runs from the date of request. These edits align with statutory timing in section 107(a)(5)(C)-(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint environmental documents and joint RODs standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must issue joint EISs, EAs, and FONSIs 'to the extent practicable' (per section 107(b)); for RODs, agencies must issue joint RODs except where it is 'inappropriate or inefficient' to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to extend the 'inappropriate or inefficient' exception to EISs, EAs, and FONSIs because the statute directs joint preparation to the extent practicable. For RODs, the tailored exception recognizes differing procedures or factors among agencies; agencies collaborating on a document should identify when a joint ROD is not appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage MOUs/letters to set roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged as a best practice to use an MOU or otherwise outline respective roles and responsibilities when multiple agencies are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ notes agencies often engage in MOUs; agencies should consider using the letter or memorandum required by §1501.7(c) to set out roles and responsibilities to facilitate an efficient process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency's consideration and use of cooperating agency analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the lead agency to give consideration to a cooperating agency's analyses, proposals, and information and to use them in the lead agency's documents to the maximum extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retained the qualifier 'to the maximum extent practicable' and the word 'proposal' to preserve clarity. CEQ declined to require lead agencies to document how and to what extent they considered cooperating agency inputs, viewing such documentation as unnecessary and potentially burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and inclusion of Indigenous Knowledge as special expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Indigenous Knowledge as a form of 'special expertise' that can qualify an agency to serve as a cooperating agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ finalized inclusion but did not add a regulatory definition of 'Indigenous Knowledge' due to diverse views and lack of consensus; agencies retain flexibility in how they approach Indigenous Knowledge. CEQ referenced existing agency approaches and interagency guidance; may consider future guidance or definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic cooperating-agency status requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead agencies are not required to grant cooperating agency status to State, Tribal, or local agencies even when they have jurisdiction by law or special expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 107(a)(3) permits but does not require designation; CEQ declines to compel lead agencies to invite or grant cooperating status because agency authorities and obligations vary and lead agencies should maintain case-by-case flexibility. CEQ also declined to add an appeal process to CEQ for non-Federal entities denied cooperating status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating agencies must meet lead agency schedules for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperating agencies are required to meet the lead agency's schedule for providing comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised paragraph (b)(7) to strike the clause that would have limited cooperating-agency comments only to matters within their jurisdiction or special expertise, to avoid undermining collaboration and to prevent unintended delays. CEQ encourages early issue identification and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach and notification obligations (combined)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall (mandatory) conduct outreach and notification, inviting likely affected agencies and governments and conducting early engagement as appropriate; the provisions on outreach and notification are combined and applied to 'agencies' (not only the lead agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ changed language from 'should' to 'shall' to remove ambiguity about optionality and to be consistent with other provisions requiring invitation of cooperating agencies. CEQ added 'as appropriate' to qualify requirements for early engagement so agencies retain flexibility where not all actions require engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of access to electronic media and primary language in outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting appropriate methods of outreach and notification, agencies must consider affected persons' ability to access electronic media and the primary language of affected persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §1501.9(c)(3) requires these considerations and CEQ notes agencies must also consider other statutory requirements (e.g., Rehabilitation Act) when selecting methods. CEQ added 'and persons' for clarity and plurality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and governmental engagement framing and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Retitle and reframe 'public involvement' as 'public and governmental engagement' and articulate purposes emphasizing 'meaningful engagement' that is interactive and collaborative, not a check-the-box exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retained 'meaningful engagement' despite concerns about subjectivity, stating agencies have flexibility to determine appropriate methods and should engage all potentially affected communities, including those with environmental justice concerns (consistent with §1500.2(d)). CEQ combined purpose and responsibility into §1501.9(a) and added a sentence clarifying the section sets forth agencies' responsibilities and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use engagement to inform level of review and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Require agencies to use public and governmental engagement to inform the level of review for and scope of analysis of a proposed action, 'as appropriate,' consistent with §1501.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added text to require engagement to inform scoping and the level of NEPA review; added cross-reference to scoping for EISs in §1502.4 and encourages using scoping for EAs where helpful, particularly when an EA relies on mitigation to reach a FONSI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology changes: 'public involvement' → 'public and governmental engagement' and 'notice' → 'notification'
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace 'public involvement' with 'public and governmental engagement' and generally replace the word 'notice' with 'notification' (except where referring to Federal Register notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The retitling is intended to reflect a more interactive and collaborative process; CEQ combined and adjusted paragraphs accordingly and clarified which provisions are obligatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/need and alternatives consultation with cooperating agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the lead agency to determine the purpose and need and alternatives in consultation with any cooperating agency, recognizing the cooperating agency's consultative role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to add a clause stating the lead agency has 'ultimate authority to finalize' purpose/need and alternatives. Instead, CEQ emphasizes collaboration and early consultation so documents meet the needs of all agencies relying on them; cooperating agencies should have a consultative role to promote efficient review and decision-making.
